headline: A 2023 law opens a one-year window for eligible low-power TV stations to apply to the FCC for Class A licenses, which give stronger spectrum protection.
what_it_does: The law sets up a one-year period in which eligible low-power television stations can apply to the Federal Communications Commission for Class A licenses. To qualify, a station must serve a media market with a limited number of TV households, broadcast a minimum number of hours, and meet other requirements. A station with a Class A license gets primary status over its spectrum, while low-power stations usually have secondary status and can be moved if the FCC reassigns that spectrum to a primary user.

who_it_affects.how: Stations that meet the market and broadcast requirements can apply during the one-year window to receive Class A status and its primary spectrum rights.

who_it_affects.group: Low-power stations that do not qualify or do not apply
who_it_affects.how: They keep their existing secondary status and can still be displaced if the FCC reallocates their spectrum to a primary user.
The agency must process applications from stations seeking Class A licenses during the window.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2023. The official summary does not list the exact start and end dates of the one-year application window.
